measures.subject: Bail exceptions for serious offenses
measures.summary: Would allow courts to deny pretrial bail, when the proof is evident or the presumption great, for terrorism, second degree murder, aggravated rape of a child, aggravated rape, grave torture, and offenses requiring service of at least 85% of a sentence, in addition to capital offenses, and would require judges to state their reasons for granting or denying bail in those cases on the record.

measures.subject: Prohibit a state property tax
measures.ballotTitle:
Shall Article II, Section 28 of the Constitution of the State of Tennessee be amended by deleting the following language from the first sentence:
In accordance with the following provisions, all property real, personal or mixed shall be subject to taxation, but the Legislature
and substituting instead the following:
In accordance with the following provisions, all property real, personal, or mixed shall be subject to taxation, but the Legislature shall not levy, authorize, or otherwise permit any state tax upon such property, and the Legislature
measures.summary: Would add language to the constitution barring the Legislature from levying, authorizing, or permitting any state tax on real, personal, or mixed property.

measures.subject: Rights of crime victims
measures.summary: Would replace the constitution's crime victims' rights section with a revised list that restates existing rights and adds others, such as fair treatment, participation in the parole process, protection from harassment, and notice of the minimum sentence and release date.

measureEffectiveNote: Under Tenn. Const. Art. XI, Sec. 3, an amendment approved by a majority of those voting on it whose yes votes also exceed half of all votes cast for governor 'shall become a part of this Constitution'; no separate effective date is set. The result is made official when state officials certify the statewide returns. No statutory certification date was confirmed; 2026-12-07 is a representative date modeled on the 2014 precedent (election Nov 4, certified Dec 8, 2014, per the Sixth Circuit's opinion in the Amendment 1 litigation).
notes: Candidates, ballot names and party labels are from the Tennessee Secretary of State's November 2026 candidate-list Excel files (Governor, U.S. Senate, U.S. House), decoded with Python's standard library; Tennessee prints non-party candidates as 'Independent'.
Congressional districts are the revised map adopted in the May 2026 Second Extraordinary Session of the 114th General Assembly; a special congressional qualifying period ended May 15, 2026.
Governor is an open seat (Bill Lee term-limited); the Class 2 U.S. Senate seat (Hagerty) is up.

Amendment ballot language is the 'Question' text on the SOS amendments page, excluding the Yes/No boxes; the SOS says the amendments are printed directly after the candidates for governor. Summaries here are our own; the Attorney General's summaries are on the source page.
Amendments pass only with more yes than no votes AND yes votes exceeding half of all votes cast for governor.
Polls close simultaneously statewide: 8:00 PM EST in Eastern counties and 7:00 PM CST in Central counties, both 01:00 UTC on Nov 4 (DST ends Nov 1).

Cross-check: WSMV (Sep 28, 2026) agrees on the governor field and the major-party nominees; it omits several independents in Senate and House races, which reads as selective coverage rather than a conflict. Ballotpedia notes Dale Braden (TN-6, independent) is not on the general ballot and Billy Cody was disqualified from the GOP primary; both consistent with the SOS lists (Cody appears as Independent in TN-1).
unconfirmed: The SOS candidate-list files carry no 'as of' date; changes after their posting were checked only through news cross-checks.

Primary results (Aug 6, 2026) could not be downloaded from the SOS (HTTP 403 on the results files); nominees were not checked against official primary returns, only against news (e.g. Bradshaw's Senate primary win).
Exact printed ballot face (name order, any amendment heading text) was not checked against a sample ballot.
Amendment certification date: no statutory deadline confirmed; 2026-12-07 is representative, based on the 2014 Dec 8 certification.
Spelling 'Knoxvile' (TN-2 Democrat Michaela Barnett's city) is a typo in the SOS file; city is not used here. WSMV spells TN-6 independent 'Angus Perdy'; the SOS file says 'Angus Purdy' (used).
